intervention_label: Comprehensive genomic profiling — paired DNA + RNA NGS (fusions, MSI, TMB) plus HER2 IHC/ISH and MMR IHC
expected_benefit: Resolves seven of eight candidate actionable axes in one pass; roughly 40% of metastatic CCA carries a targetable alteration the panel would surface.
key_risks: None beyond a tissue draw; archival FFPE or 10-20 unstained slides, or ctDNA when tissue is limited.
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials: YES (a positive call opens the FGFR2/IDH1/HER2/BRAF/NTRK/RET/KRAS-G12C trial menu); no modality or toxicity constraints engaged.
guideline_status: NCCN Hepatobiliary/Biliary Tract Cancers v2.2025 advises CGP at diagnosis of unresectable/metastatic disease.
rationale_summary: No molecular profiling was supplied, so every therapeutic axis in this case is unmeasured and the confirmatory test is itself the first action. All five personas treated comprehensive genomic profiling as the rank-1 gate; none picked it as a therapy because it is the shared workup, not a feature-targeting drug. A single paired DNA+RNA panel resolves FGFR2 fusion, IDH1 R132, BRAF V600E, KRAS G12C, NTRK/RET fusion, MSI and TMB at once, and an RNA-based fusion read matters because DNA-only calling misses a subset of FGFR2 fusions with intronic breakpoints. HER2 needs IHC with reflex ISH rather than an NGS copy-number call, and MMR IHC is the fastest orthogonal dMMR read, so the workup pairs the panel with those protein assays. Every ranked therapeutic below is foreclosed until this returns positive for its feature.
open_questions: Tumor subsite (intrahepatic vs extrahepatic vs perihilar/distal) is unspecified and shifts the pre-test probability of FGFR2/IDH1 (intrahepatic-skewed) versus HER2 (extrahepatic/gallbladder-skewed).
Whether archival tissue is adequate or a fresh biopsy / ctDNA parallel is needed.
likelihood_of_effect: Diagnostic certainty — resolves which of up to eight feature-conditional pathways is reachable; roughly 40% prior probability of a targetable hit across the panel.
toxicity_burden: Low (none — diagnostic test on tissue or blood)
overall: The non-toxic gate that opens every feature-conditional rec below; a paired DNA+RNA panel plus HER2 IHC/ISH and MMR IHC resolves seven of eight axes in one pass.

intervention_label: Ivosidenib (if IDH1 R132 confirmed on tumor NGS)
expected_benefit: ClarIDHy: median PFS 2.7 vs 1.4 mo, PFS HR 0.37 (95% CI 0.25-0.54, p<0.0001); ORR only 2%, so the realistic goal is delayed progression rather than tumor shrinkage.
key_risks: QT prolongation (class effect; grade 3 ~1%; needs baseline and on-treatment ECGs)
Ascites (grade 3+ ~7%, matching placebo)
Fatigue (grade 3 ~3%)
preference_alignment: matches balanced efficacy/toxicity weight (oral, near-placebo grade 3+ profile): YES; matches prefers_trials: YES (open registration trial NCT02989857).
guideline_status: NCCN BTC v2.2025 category 2A (subsequent-line IDH1-mutant); ESMO 2023 BTC recommended.
rationale_summary: If the IDH1 R132 hotspot reads positive, ivosidenib is the only option here built on a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled phase 3, and the conservative, critic, and concensusite all led with it on that strength. The honest limit, which the critic pinned down, is that the registered ITT OS missed at HR 0.69 (p=0.060) and the quoted 0.46 is an RPSFT crossover adjustment after 70% of placebo patients crossed over, so the survival case rests on a sensitivity analysis, not a clean result. The risktaker dissented on rank order, arguing that an ORR-2% option should not lead over the higher-response fusion agents once a test reads positive, and the advocate flagged that a balanced preference weight does not license a safety-first tiebreaker; both objections concern ranking, not whether to use ivosidenib in IDH1-mutant disease. IDH1 R132 runs 15-20% in intrahepatic CCA, among the likeliest positives the panel returns. The board endorsement of the drug itself was unanimous.
open_questions: Whether organ-function labs support QT monitoring (no baseline ECG/electrolytes supplied).
Subsite: IDH1 is intrahepatic-skewed and subsite is unspecified.
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate — only RCT-grade evidence here (ClarIDHy PFS HR 0.37) but the absolute single-agent effect is small (mPFS 2.7 vs 1.4 mo, ORR 2%); benefit is disease control, not shrinkage.
toxicity_burden: Low (QT prolongation ~1% G3, ascites ~7% G3+, fatigue ~3% G3; near-placebo profile)

counter_productive_moa.description: No counter-productive vector; dissent is about depth-of-response rank order, not mechanism.

overall: The cleanest evidence in the set on a randomized phase 3, but the single-agent payoff is disease stabilization rather than shrinkage; foreclosed if IDH1 R132 is wild-type.
scenario_label: If IDH1 R132 confirmed on tumor NGS

intervention_label: Futibatinib (if FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed on RNA-based CGP)
expected_benefit: FOENIX-CCA2: ORR 42% (95% CI 32-52), median OS 21.7 mo, only 2% discontinued for toxicity; irreversible binding holds against some pemigatinib-resistant kinase-domain mutations.
key_risks: Hyperphosphatemia (on-target FGFR class effect; grade 3 ~30%, needs active phosphate management)
Increased AST (grade 3+ ~7%)
Stomatitis and fatigue (grade 3+ ~6% each)
preference_alignment: matches balanced weight (oral, low 2% discontinuation): PARTIAL (30% grade-3 hyperphosphatemia is the offsetting load); matches prefers_trials: YES (active FGFR2 trials including the next-gen TYRA-200 study NCT06160752 for later resistance).
guideline_status: NCCN BTC v2.2025 category 2A (subsequent-line FGFR2 fusion); higher ESMO-MCBS v1.1 score than pemigatinib (3 vs 2).
rationale_summary: On a confirmed FGFR2 fusion, this is the highest-yield molecular axis to chase in this disease (10-15% of intrahepatic CCA), and the critic trusts it most among single-arm options because FOENIX-CCA2 and FIGHT-202 are two independent trials converging on the same effect direction in centrally confirmed fusions. The concensusite seated it ahead of pemigatinib on the higher ESMO-MCBS score and the documented activity against pemigatinib-resistant kinase-domain mutations. The conservative dissented within the lane, reversing the order on toxicity: grade 3 hyperphosphatemia reached 30% on futibatinib against essentially none on pemigatinib, and at comparable ORR the conservative takes the lower-grade burden. The honest limit, named by the critic and concensusite, is that the evidence is single-arm phase 2 with a surrogate ORR endpoint and no randomized comparator. An RNA-based fusion call is the gate because DNA-only panels can miss FGFR2 fusions.
open_questions: Subsite: FOENIX eligibility was built on intrahepatic CCA; a non-intrahepatic primary weakens the fit.
Whether phosphate-management infrastructure is in place for the 30% grade-3 hyperphosphatemia.
likelihood_of_effect: High in FGFR2-fusion subset — ORR 42% (FOENIX-CCA2) with cross-trial concordance to pemigatinib (FIGHT-202); the nearest thing to replication in this dossier.

counter_productive_moa.description: Hyperphosphatemia is on-target and manageable, not counter-productive to efficacy; conservative dissent is toxicity-burden, not mechanism.

overall: Targets the highest-yield CCA axis with cross-trial-concordant 42% ORR; the on-target 30% grade-3 hyperphosphatemia is the tradeoff against the gentler pemigatinib.
scenario_label: If FGFR2 fusion/rearrangement confirmed on RNA-based CGP

expected_benefit: FIGHT-202: ORR 35.5% (95% CI 26.5-45.4); reported OS 21.1 mo is immature (40 events at cutoff); hyperphosphatemia 55% any-grade with no grade 3-4.
key_risks: Hyperphosphatemia (55% any-grade, on-target; no grade 3-4) with reflex hypophosphatemia (grade 3+ ~12%)
Serous retinal detachment (~4%; needs scheduled ophthalmologic checks)
Nail and skin toxicity, alopecia, dysgeusia (any-grade ~40-46%)
preference_alignment: matches balanced weight (oral, no grade 3-4 hyperphosphatemia): YES; matches prefers_trials: YES.
guideline_status: NCCN BTC v2.2025 category 2A (subsequent-line FGFR2 fusion); ESMO recommended; first FGFR inhibitor approved in CCA.
rationale_summary: Pemigatinib is the second guideline-endorsed FGFR2 option and shares the exact FGFR2-fusion gate with futibatinib, so the choice between them is a within-lane call once the fusion confirms. The conservative ranked it above futibatinib specifically on the toxicity axis: its hyperphosphatemia ran 55% any-grade with no grade 3-4 events against futibatinib's 30% grade 3, and it carries the longest post-approval record as the first FGFR inhibitor approved in the indication. The critic and concensusite kept it just below futibatinib because futibatinib documents activity in the post-pemigatinib resistance setting and carries the higher ESMO-MCBS score, though the critic noted the score is built from two separate single-arm trials with no head-to-head and cannot truly adjudicate the order. Both rows ride a surrogate ORR endpoint behind an accelerated approval, and the reported OS is immature. Serous retinal detachment is the item that needs scheduled ophthalmologic monitoring.
open_questions: Subsite unspecified against an intrahepatic-built indication.
No head-to-head versus futibatinib exists, so the within-lane order rests on cross-trial toxicity and MCBS judgment.
likelihood_of_effect: High in FGFR2-fusion subset — ORR 35.5% (FIGHT-202), concordant with futibatinib; gentler grade-3 toxicity profile but immature OS.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (hypophosphatemia G3+ ~12%, serous retinal detachment ~4%, PPE/nail toxicity; hyperphosphatemia 55% any-grade with no G3-4)

counter_productive_moa.description: On-target FGFR phosphate dysregulation is managed, not counter-productive to the antitumor goal.

overall: The same FGFR2-fusion gate as futibatinib with a gentler grade-3 profile and longer track record; the within-lane choice turns on the toxicity-versus-resistance-coverage tradeoff once the fusion confirms.

intervention_label: Zanidatamab (if HER2 IHC 3+ with reflex ISH confirmed)
expected_benefit: HERIZON-BTC-01: confirmed ORR 41.3% (95% CI 30.4-52.8), median DoR 12.9 mo in HER2-amplified, IHC 2+/3+ biliary tract cancer.
key_risks: Decreased ejection fraction (HER2-directed cardiac class effect; grade 3 ~3%; needs baseline and serial echo)
Diarrhea (grade 3 ~5%)
Infusion-related reactions (~35% any-grade)
preference_alignment: matches balanced weight (manageable cardiac signal with standard echo algorithm): YES; matches prefers_trials: YES (first-line HERIZON successor NCT06282575 if treatment-naive); IV route, but no modality veto was set.
guideline_status: NCCN BTC v2.2025 category 2A (subsequent-line HER2-positive); the only dedicated biliary HER2 trial behind a guideline listing.
rationale_summary: On confirmed HER2 positivity, zanidatamab is the lead HER2 choice across the board because HERIZON-BTC-01 is a dedicated biliary trial rather than a pan-tumor basket, and the biparatopic design beat trastuzumab plus pertuzumab in preclinical HER2 models. The conservative preferred it over trastuzumab deruxtecan on a straightforward safety argument: its grade 3 ejection-fraction drop sat at 3% with an established monitoring algorithm, against T-DXd's 10.5% adjudicated ILD with three treatment-related deaths. The gate is HER2 IHC with reflex ISH on the trial's own 4B5 scoring, not an NGS copy-number call standing in for the protein read, and HER2 skews toward extrahepatic and gallbladder disease, so a positive result depends on a subsite intake never specified. The evidence is single-arm phase 2b behind an accelerated approval. No baseline cardiac function was supplied for the ejection-fraction signal.
open_questions: Subsite drives HER2 prevalence and is unspecified.
No baseline cardiac assessment supplied for the 3% grade-3 ejection-fraction signal.
likelihood_of_effect: High in HER2-positive subset — confirmed ORR 41.3% with mDoR 12.9 mo in the only dedicated biliary HER2 trial (HERIZON-BTC-01).
toxicity_burden: Low (decreased ejection fraction G3 ~3%, diarrhea G3 ~5%; standard echo monitoring)

counter_productive_moa.description: No counter-productive vector; HER2 blockade is direct and on-target with a managed cardiac signal.

overall: The guideline-endorsed HER2 lead on dedicated biliary-trial data; gated on HER2 IHC/ISH (not an NGS copy-number call) and on a subsite that drives HER2 prevalence.

intervention_label: Dabrafenib + trametinib (if BRAF V600E confirmed on NGS/PCR)
expected_benefit: ROAR biliary cohort: ORR 47% (95% CI 31-62), median PFS 9.0 mo; tumor-agnostic BRAF V600E label gives a second route to treat.
key_risks: Pyrexia (characteristic combination effect; ~19% any-grade; drove most treatment-related serious AEs)
Treatment-related serious AEs ~21%; any serious AE ~40%
Increased gamma-glutamyltransferase (grade 3+ ~12%)
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials and oral modality: YES; tension with the tolerability half of the balanced weight (40% serious AE rate, frequent pyrexia, heavier than the higher-ranked oral agents).
guideline_status: NCCN BTC v2.2025 category 2A (subsequent-line) plus the tumor-agnostic FDA label.
rationale_summary: A confirmed BRAF V600E opens a doublet endorsed by both NCCN and the tumor-agnostic label, with a strong 47% ORR in the ROAR biliary cohort. The conservative knows the toxicity cold from years of melanoma use and values the predictable pyrexia playbook; the concensusite anchored it on cross-society and cross-label convergence. The advocate did not veto it but ranked it below the gentler oral agents because the 40% serious-AE rate and frequent pyrexia sit heavier against a balanced preference weight. The hard gate, which the risktaker and conservative both stressed, is a true V600E confirmed by NGS or PCR: a VE1 IHC screen alone is suggestive only, and class-2/3 BRAF alterations do not qualify. BRAF V600E appears in only 1-5% of biliary tract cancer and the cohort is small (n=43) and single-arm.
open_questions: Whether the panel reads a true V600E versus a non-actionable class-2/3 BRAF alteration.
Whether the pyrexia-management infrastructure the guideline presumes is in place.
likelihood_of_effect: High in BRAF V600E subset — ORR 47%, mPFS 9.0 mo (ROAR), but on a small single-arm basket cohort (n=43) at 1-5% prevalence.
toxicity_burden: Moderate (pyrexia ~19%, treatment-related serious AEs ~21%, GGT increase G3+ ~12%; any serious AE ~40%)

counter_productive_moa.description: No counter-productive vector; the pyrexia/serious-AE load is a patient-AE burden, not a goal-blunting mechanism.

overall: Strong 47% ORR on a true V600E with dual guideline-plus-agnostic-label backing; the higher serious-AE and pyrexia load is what keeps it below the gentler oral options at equal agreement.
scenario_label: If BRAF V600E confirmed on NGS/PCR

intervention_label: Larotrectinib (if NTRK1/2/3 fusion confirmed on RNA-based CGP)
expected_benefit: Pooled phase 1/2 (NAVIGATE and others): ORR 79% (95% CI 72-85), median DoR 35.2 mo, median OS 44.4 mo across tumor types; grade 3 AEs 13%, grade 4 <1%.
key_risks: Grade 3 AEs ~13%, grade 4 <1%, no treatment-related deaths (gentlest profile in the dossier)
Increased ALT (grade 3+ ~3%)
Acquired NTRK kinase-domain resistance mutations documented over time
preference_alignment: matches balanced weight (oral, low grade 3+ rate, durable responses): YES; matches prefers_trials: YES (open basket NCT02576431).
guideline_status: NCCN BTC v2.2025 listed via the tumor-agnostic NTRK label.
rationale_summary: If the fusion panel returns an NTRK fusion, larotrectinib offers the single largest response signal in the dossier (ORR 79%) at the gentlest toxicity profile, which is why the risktaker led with it on expected effect and the conservative and advocate gave it a top-three slot on tolerability. The dissents are about rank, not the drug: the critic objected that the 79% is a pooled cross-tumor basket with no biliary cohort, the thinnest indication base on the board to seat first, and the concensusite argued that seating a sub-1% NTRK read above the 15-20% IDH1 and 10-15% FGFR2 axes inverts the testing priority the guidelines actually set. The advocate, reading the preference file plainly, also pulled back the rank because a sub-1% read is the one the patient is least likely to ever act on. The evidence is single-arm and pooled across tumor types with no CCA-specific subgroup, and acquired NTRK resistance mutations are documented. An RNA-based assay is the gate.
open_questions: No CCA-specific subgroup ORR; biliary magnitude is inferred from the cross-tumor pool.
Sub-1% prevalence makes a positive read unlikely.
likelihood_of_effect: High in NTRK-fusion subset — ORR 79% pooled, mDoR 35.2 mo; but sub-1% prevalence and no CCA-specific cohort temper the prior.
toxicity_burden: Low (grade 3 AEs ~13%, grade 4 <1%, ALT increase ~3%; no treatment-related deaths)

counter_productive_moa.description: Critic dissented on cross-tumor extrapolation; acquired NTRK kinase-domain resistance can blunt durability over time.

overall: The largest response signal anywhere here if the rare fusion confirms, but the evidence is cross-tumor pooled with no biliary cohort and prevalence is sub-1%.
scenario_label: If NTRK1/2/3 fusion confirmed on RNA-based CGP

expected_benefit: KEYNOTE-158: MSI-H/dMMR ORR 34.3% (95% CI 28.3-40.8); TMB-high (>=10 mut/Mb) ORR 29% (95% CI 21-39); durable responses in responders.
key_risks: Immune-mediated grade 3-5 TRAEs ~14.6% (one treatment-related death, pneumonia)
Immune-mediated colitis, pneumonitis, endocrinopathies (class effects with an established management algorithm)
preference_alignment: matches prefers_trials: YES (open MSI-H/TMB-high basket NCT02628067); IV route with no modality veto, so not penalized.
guideline_status: NCCN-listed via the MSI-H/dMMR and TMB-high tumor-agnostic labels.
rationale_summary: For an MSI-H/dMMR or TMB-high tumor, pembrolizumab can deliver the durable long-tail response that chemotherapy does not, and the advocate surfaced it as the immunotherapy option whose IV route should not be penalized when no modality veto is on file. The conservative and critic both qualified rather than dissented: the immune-mediated toxicity is well-characterized with an established algorithm (grade 3-5 TRAEs 14.6%), but neither KEYNOTE-158 row reports a CCA-specific subgroup ORR, so the biliary magnitude is inferred from a 27-tumor pool the patient enters on the biomarker alone. MSI-H/dMMR is uncommon in biliary tract cancer (roughly 1-3%) but decision-changing when present, and MMR IHC with reflex MSI-PCR is the fastest orthogonal gate. A confirmed MSI-H or TMB-high read admits the patient to the labeled indication.
open_questions: No CCA-specific subgroup ORR published for either the MSI-H or TMB-high read.
Whether organ-function baseline supports immune-AE monitoring (none supplied).
likelihood_of_effect: Moderate in MSI-H/TMB-high subset — ORR ~29-34% (KEYNOTE-158) with durable responders, but no CCA-specific subgroup and ~1-3% prevalence.
toxicity_burden: Low (immune-mediated grade 3-5 TRAEs ~14.6%; one treatment-related death)

counter_productive_moa.description: No counter-productive vector at this evidence depth; checkpoint resistance is possible but the dissent was preference/evidence-flavored, not mechanistic.

overall: Offers a durable immunotherapy tail if MSI-H/dMMR or TMB-high confirms, but the biliary magnitude is inferred from a cross-tumor basket with no CCA-specific subgroup.
scenario_label: If MSI-H/dMMR or TMB-high (>=10 mut/Mb) confirmed

intervention_label: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (if HER2 IHC 3+ confirmed) — kept to document the board's veto
expected_benefit: DESTINY-PanTumor02 biliary cohort: ORR 22% (95% CI 10.6-37.6, n=41) overall; 61.3% in the post-hoc central IHC 3+ subgroup with mDoR 22.1 mo.
key_risks: Adjudicated drug-related ILD/pneumonitis 10.5% with three treatment-related deaths (dominant risk)
Drug-related grade 3+ AEs ~40.8% study-wide
Nausea and other GI effects (study-wide, not separated for the biliary cohort)
preference_alignment: no modality or toxicity veto on file; but the conservative's clinical veto rests on the absence of a pulmonary baseline to gate the ILD risk against.
guideline_status: Off-label / pan-tumor basket route into BTC; not the guideline-endorsed HER2 lead (zanidatamab holds that on dedicated biliary data).
rationale_summary: T-DXd is kept in the table at not_recommended so the reader sees what the board considered and rejected, rather than dropping the veto silently. The conservative issued a formal veto on toxicity grounds: adjudicated drug-related ILD ran 10.5% with three treatment-related deaths, and intake supplied no pulmonary baseline, no DLCO, and no organ-function labs to gate against, so the uncharacterized severe long-tail cannot be safely entered. The veto is explicitly contingent: it lifts only on a documented HER2 IHC 3+ read plus a baseline pulmonary assessment and a written ILD-monitoring plan. The critic listed T-DXd at rank 5 to flag, not endorse, noting that the eye-catching 61.3% is a post-hoc unadjusted IHC 3+ subgroup, not the registered biliary-cohort result of 22% (n=41). The risktaker would chase the 61.3% on a true 3+ tumor but agreed it stays gated. With zanidatamab covering the HER2 lane on dedicated biliary-trial data at a 3% cardiac signal, the board's HER2 lead is zanidatamab and T-DXd is held in reserve behind the veto conditions.
open_questions: No pulmonary baseline / DLCO supplied to gate the 10.5% ILD risk.
Biliary-cohort AE rates are reported study-wide, not cohort-specific.
The 61.3% rests on a small post-hoc IHC 3+ slice with investigator-assessed response.
likelihood_of_effect: Low-to-moderate as registered (biliary-cohort ORR 22%); the 61.3% IHC 3+ figure is a post-hoc unadjusted subgroup, not the pre-specified endpoint.
toxicity_burden: High (adjudicated ILD/pneumonitis 10.5% with three treatment-related deaths; grade 3+ AEs ~40.8% study-wide)

counter_productive_moa.description: Conservative veto stands on the uncharacterized ILD long-tail; treatment-related deaths make the toxicity itself the goal-defeating mechanism here.

overall: Not recommended as the HER2 lead: a documented ILD signal with three treatment-related deaths and no pulmonary baseline to gate against, where zanidatamab covers HER2 more safely on dedicated biliary data.
scenario_label: If HER2 IHC 3+ confirmed (held behind the board veto)
